title: WHY THE PANAMA CANAL NEEDS WATER LOCKS
subject: geography

beats.narration: A ship crossing Panama does not cut through the continent. It climbs over it: twenty-six meters up a staircase made of water.
beats.claim: the canal lifts ships about 26 meters above sea level to cross the terrain
beats.visual_question: why does a ship need stairs?
beats.visual_answer: a map of Panama with the canal stepping up over the ridge

beats.narration: Panama's spine is hard rock, and the Pacific tide swings meters twice a day. A sea-level ditch was impossible, so the canal climbs over the ridge instead.
beats.claim: terrain and tide made a sea-level canal impractical
beats.visual_question: why not just dig straight through?
beats.visual_answer: a rock ridge and a swinging tide blocking a flat channel

beats.narration: Each lock is a concrete chamber that fills by gravity alone. Lake Gatun pours downhill through the valves, lifting the ship. There are no pumps.
beats.claim: locks fill by gravity from Lake Gatun with no pumping
beats.visual_question: what lifts forty thousand tonnes of ship?
beats.visual_answer: gravity-fed water pouring from the lake into the chamber

beats.narration: But every transit pays a water toll. Each lockage dumps millions of liters of fresh water out to sea, and only rain can refill the lake.
beats.claim: each ship transit discharges huge volumes of freshwater to the ocean
beats.visual_question: what does each transit cost the lake?
beats.visual_answer: fresh water draining lock by lock toward both oceans

beats.narration: When drought shrinks the lake, the canal must cut drafts and daily transits. A queue of world shipping now waits on rainfall.
beats.claim: drought lowers Gatun and forces transit restrictions
beats.visual_question: what happens when the staircase runs low?
beats.visual_answer: a falling lake level and a shrinking draft line

beats.narration: That is why the new locks recycle about sixty percent of every drop. Gravity does the lifting, and every saved liter keeps the ships climbing.
beats.claim: the expanded locks recycle roughly 60 percent of lockage water
beats.visual_question: how does the staircase keep running?
beats.visual_answer: water-saving basins returning about sixty percent of each fill
